quests.sentence: Because the roads were icy she decided not to drive
quests.correctAnswer: Because the roads were icy, she decided not to drive.
quests.hint: The 'because' clause comes before the main sentence - what separates them?
quests.explanation: When a subordinate clause beginning with 'because' comes before the main clause, a comma separates them.

quests.sentence: Since she had extra time she decided to read a few more chapters
quests.correctAnswer: Since she had extra time, she decided to read a few more chapters.
quests.hint: When does the comma come after a 'since' clause?
quests.explanation: Subordinate clauses starting with 'since' that appear before the main clause are followed by a comma.

quests.sentence: Because the venue was fully booked they held the event in the garden
quests.correctAnswer: Because the venue was fully booked, they held the event in the garden.
quests.hint: The reason comes first - use a comma before the result.
quests.explanation: An introductory 'because' clause must be followed by a comma before the main clause begins.

quests.sentence: When the bell rang all the students rushed out into the hallway
quests.correctAnswer: When the bell rang, all the students rushed out into the hallway.
quests.hint: 'When' starts a subordinate clause - what follows when that clause comes first?
quests.explanation: Introductory time clauses beginning with 'when' are separated from the main clause by a comma.

quests.sentence: While we were waiting for the train a street musician began to play
quests.correctAnswer: While we were waiting for the train, a street musician began to play.
quests.hint: 'While' introduces a background action - use a comma after the clause.
quests.explanation: Clauses beginning with 'while' that precede the main clause are set off with a comma.

quests.sentence: After the presentation ended the audience applauded for several minutes
quests.correctAnswer: After the presentation ended, the audience applauded for several minutes.
quests.hint: The 'after' clause sets the time - mark where it ends.
quests.explanation: Introductory 'after' clauses are followed by a comma when they appear before the main clause.

quests.sentence: If you finish your homework early you can watch television
quests.correctAnswer: If you finish your homework early, you can watch television.
quests.hint: 'If' opens a condition - the comma comes right before the result.
quests.explanation: Conditional clauses beginning with 'if' that precede the main clause must be followed by a comma.

quests.sentence: Unless you book a table in advance you may not get a seat
quests.correctAnswer: Unless you book a table in advance, you may not get a seat.
quests.hint: 'Unless' introduces a negative condition - mark where the condition ends.
quests.explanation: Introductory clauses with 'unless' are separated from the main clause by a comma.

quests.sentence: If the rain continues the outdoor concert will be moved indoors
quests.correctAnswer: If the rain continues, the outdoor concert will be moved indoors.
quests.hint: A conditional 'if' clause opening the sentence takes a comma at its end.
quests.explanation: The comma after an introductory 'if' clause shows where the condition ends and the result begins.

quests.sentence: Although the film was long it kept everyone's attention throughout
quests.correctAnswer: Although the film was long, it kept everyone's attention throughout.
quests.hint: The concessive 'although' clause comes first - separate it from the main idea.
quests.explanation: Introductory concessive clauses starting with 'although' are followed by a comma before the main clause.

quests.sentence: Even though she was nervous she delivered a confident speech
quests.correctAnswer: Even though she was nervous, she delivered a confident speech.
quests.hint: 'Even though' is a two-word subordinator - the comma comes after its clause.
quests.explanation: Multi-word subordinators like 'even though' introduce subordinate clauses; when placed first, the clause ends with a comma.

quests.sentence: Although the price was high the quality made it worth every penny
quests.correctAnswer: Although the price was high, the quality made it worth every penny.
quests.hint: Contrast is set up by 'although' - the comma follows the contrasting clause.
quests.explanation: When 'although' introduces a contrasting idea before the main clause, a comma marks the boundary between them.

quests.sentence: I'll be ready in five minutes she promised just give me a moment
quests.correctAnswer: "I'll be ready in five minutes," she promised, "just give me a moment."
quests.hint: The attribution 'she promised' interrupts the quote - it goes between the two halves.
quests.explanation: When an attribution splits a quotation, place a comma (and closing quote) before it and a comma (and opening quote) after it. Lowercase the second half since it is the same sentence.

quests.sentence: The best way to learn he insisted is to make mistakes and try again
quests.correctAnswer: "The best way to learn," he insisted, "is to make mistakes and try again."
quests.hint: He insists in the middle - put the attribution between the two parts of the quote.
quests.explanation: A split quotation has its attribution phrase set between two quotation segments, each requiring its own quotation marks. A comma appears before and after the attribution.

quests.sentence: We should leave now she urged otherwise we'll miss the first act
quests.correctAnswer: "We should leave now," she urged, "otherwise we'll miss the first act."
quests.hint: She urges between two parts of her own sentence.
quests.explanation: In a split quotation where the attribution divides a single sentence, each half sits inside its own quotation marks and commas flank the attribution.

quests.sentence: She left the office early because she had a dentist appointment.
quests.correctAnswer: She left the office early because she had a dentist appointment.
quests.hint: When 'because' comes after the main clause, do you still need a comma?
quests.explanation: When a 'because' clause follows the main clause, no comma is needed. The comma rule for introductory clauses only applies when the subordinate clause comes first.

quests.sentence: He takes a walk every morning, because it clears his mind.
quests.correctAnswer: He takes a walk every morning because it clears his mind.
quests.hint: When the reason clause follows the main clause, the comma is not needed.
quests.explanation: Removing an unnecessary comma between a main clause and a following 'because' clause is the correct edit. No comma is needed when the subordinate clause comes after the main clause.

quests.sentence: They stayed up late, because they wanted to watch the meteor shower.
quests.correctAnswer: They stayed up late because they wanted to watch the meteor shower.
quests.hint: The reason follows the main action - is the comma correct here?
quests.explanation: A comma before 'because' is incorrect when 'because' connects the main clause to its reason. Remove the comma to produce natural, standard English.

quests.sentence: My uncle who lives in Canada is visiting us next week
quests.correctAnswer: My uncle, who lives in Canada, is visiting us next week.
quests.hint: Does 'who lives in Canada' tell us which uncle? If the reader already knows who, set the clause off with commas.
quests.explanation: A 'who' clause that adds non-essential information about an already-identified noun is non-restrictive and is set off with commas.

quests.sentence: The head chef who trained in Paris creates a new menu every season
quests.correctAnswer: The head chef, who trained in Paris, creates a new menu every season.
quests.hint: There is one head chef - the Paris detail is extra information, not identification.
quests.explanation: When a 'who' clause gives background detail rather than identifying which person, commas are placed around it.

quests.sentence: Our school principal who has worked here for twenty years is retiring this June
quests.correctAnswer: Our school principal, who has worked here for twenty years, is retiring this June.
quests.hint: We already know who the principal is - the clause adds a fact, not identification.
quests.explanation: Non-restrictive 'who' clauses that provide extra detail about a specific, already-known person require commas on both sides.

quests.sentence: The old bridge which was built in 1887 is now a protected monument
quests.correctAnswer: The old bridge, which was built in 1887, is now a protected monument.
quests.hint: Does 'which was built in 1887' tell you which bridge, or add extra history about it?
quests.explanation: 'Which' introduces non-restrictive clauses about things. When the clause gives extra information, not identification, enclose it in commas.

quests.sentence: Her laptop which she bought just last year is already outdated
quests.correctAnswer: Her laptop, which she bought just last year, is already outdated.
quests.hint: She has one laptop - the detail about when it was bought is extra.
quests.explanation: The 'which' clause provides non-essential detail about a specific item and must be set off with commas.

quests.sentence: The company's main product which won three industry awards last year has seen falling sales
quests.correctAnswer: The company's main product, which won three industry awards last year, has seen falling sales.
quests.hint: There is one main product - the award detail is bonus information.
quests.explanation: Non-restrictive 'which' clauses add detail without identifying the noun. They are always surrounded by commas.

quests.sentence: Because it was her birthday she chose the restaurant and her family paid for the meal
quests.correctAnswer: Because it was her birthday, she chose the restaurant, and her family paid for the meal.
quests.hint: Two commas are needed: one after the 'because' clause, and one before 'and' joining two main clauses.
quests.explanation: An introductory 'because' clause takes a comma, and 'and' joining two independent clauses also takes a comma before it.

quests.sentence: When the power went out we lit candles but we couldn't read in the dim light
quests.correctAnswer: When the power went out, we lit candles, but we couldn't read in the dim light.
quests.hint: Fix the introductory clause first, then deal with the compound sentence.
quests.explanation: An introductory 'when' clause is followed by a comma, and 'but' joining two independent clauses also requires a comma before it.

quests.sentence: Although the fee was high we enrolled in the course and we have no regrets
quests.correctAnswer: Although the fee was high, we enrolled in the course, and we have no regrets.
quests.hint: Three clauses, two boundary commas - find where each one belongs.
quests.explanation: The introductory 'although' clause takes a comma, and 'and' connecting the two main clauses also takes a comma.

quests.sentence: If you see Marco my old university roommate please say hello from me
quests.correctAnswer: If you see Marco, my old university roommate, please say hello from me.
quests.hint: Two punctuation tasks: end the 'if' clause, then set off the appositive.
quests.explanation: An introductory 'if' clause ends with a comma, and the appositive 'my old university roommate' takes commas around it.

quests.sentence: The director shouted cut and everyone on set relaxed immediately
quests.correctAnswer: The director shouted, "Cut!" and everyone on set relaxed immediately.
quests.hint: The director shouts one word with force - mark the shout, then continue the story.
quests.explanation: A one-word exclamatory quotation ends with an exclamation mark inside the closing quote. 'And' here does not join two full independent clauses, so no additional comma is needed before it.

quests.sentence: While the technician was fixing the printer the whole office waited and nobody could print their documents
quests.correctAnswer: While the technician was fixing the printer, the whole office waited, and nobody could print their documents.
quests.hint: Three clauses: an introductory 'while' clause, then two main clauses joined by 'and.'
quests.explanation: After the introductory 'while' clause a comma is placed, and before 'and' that joins two independent clauses another comma is needed.
